## Summary

The project is the **Spring PetClinic REST** application, built with **Maven** (`pom.xml` + `mvnw` wrapper present; no Gradle). The "business-day rule" for registration dates is implemented in the owner-creation REST controller, and there is one acceptance test asserting the invariant plus a duplicate helper in the test base class.

## 1 & 2. The adjustment logic (where it lives)

The logic lives directly in the REST controller (not a separate service/util) as a private method `toBusinessDay`.

**File:** `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`

The method (lines 495-510):
```java
495	    /**
496	     * Rolls a registration date forward to a business day. A registration date must fall on a
497	     * business day, so when the supplied or defaulted date lands on a Saturday or Sunday it is
498	     * moved forward to the following Monday; a weekday is returned unchanged. Every value derived
499	     * from the registration date (such as the membership number's year segment) and the daily
500	     * create-limit therefore use the adjusted date.
501	     *
502	     * @param date the effective registration date, whether supplied or defaulted to the server date
503	     * @return the same date when it is a weekday, otherwise the next Monday
504	     */
505	    private LocalDate toBusinessDay(LocalDate date) {
506	        while (date.getDayOfWeek() == DayOfWeek.SATURDAY || date.getDayOfWeek() == DayOfWeek.SUNDAY) {
507	            date = date.plusDays(1);
508	        }
509	        return date;
510	    }
```

Where it is invoked — inside `addOwner(...)` (lines 183-187). Note it validates, defaults a null date to `LocalDate.now()`, then rolls to a business day:
```java
183	        validateRegistrationDate(owner.getRegistrationDate());
184	        if (owner.getRegistrationDate() == null) {
185	            owner.setRegistrationDate(LocalDate.now());
186	        }
187	        owner.setRegistrationDate(toBusinessDay(owner.getRegistrationDate()));
```

The adjusted date then feeds downstream logic: the daily create-limit check (`countOwnersRegisteredOn`, lines 200-204), the `OwnerDailyLimitException`, the membership-number year segment (`OwnerMapper.java`), age band, and membership tenure.

## 4. Public holiday handling

Important finding: **there is NO public-holiday handling in the production/main code.** The production `toBusinessDay` (above) skips **weekends only** — Saturday/Sunday. A grep for `holiday`/`HOLIDAYS` across `src/main` returns nothing.

Holiday handling exists **only in the test code**, as pinned reference data, in the acceptance base class:

**File:** `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceBase.java`
```java
239	/** Fixed public holidays the business-day roll skips (year of the run). */
240	protected static final Set<LocalDate> HOLIDAYS = Set.of(
241		LocalDate.parse("2026-01-01"), LocalDate.parse("2026-01-26"),
242		LocalDate.parse("2026-04-25"), LocalDate.parse("2026-12-25"), LocalDate.parse("2026-12-28"));
...
267	/** Roll a date forward over weekends and pinned holidays to the next business day. */
268	protected LocalDate toBusinessDay(LocalDate d) {
269		while (d.getDayOfWeek() == DayOfWeek.SATURDAY || d.getDayOfWeek() == DayOfWeek.SUNDAY
270				|| HOLIDAYS.contains(d)) {
271			d = d.plusDays(1);
272		}
273		return d;
274	}
```

There is a discrepancy worth flagging: the test-side helper and the `AcceptanceTest` javadoc both claim the registration date "rolls past public holidays as well as weekends," but the production `toBusinessDay` only handles weekends. The test's own `toBusinessDay` helper (lines 268-274) is not actually called by the assertion in `AcceptanceTest` (see below), so this mismatch is not currently exercised.

## 3. Existing tests for the business-day adjustment

Only one test targets this. It asserts the weaker weekday invariant rather than an exact rolled date.

**File:** `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceTest.java` (full file):

11	 * the invariant that subsumes it: the default registrationDate is never a Saturday or Sunday. */

This is a `@SpringBootTest` + `@AutoConfigureMockMvc` black-box style test (config in `AcceptanceBase`, lines 47-51). It creates an owner via MockMvc, re-fetches it, and asserts the returned `registrationDate` is not a weekend. The `toBusinessDay` helper (with holidays) in `AcceptanceBase` is defined but not referenced by this assertion.

There is no dedicated unit test that directly invokes the controller's private `toBusinessDay`, and no test asserting holiday rolling behavior against the server.
